subject.title: fix(agents): hard-deadline runtime auth refresh to prevent gateway deadlock

question: Should this auth-timeout PR require side-effect-safe timeout ownership before merge?
rationale: The patch addresses a real availability failure, but the current non-cancelling timeouts change auth-provider and session-state concurrency in a way that green tests do not settle.

options.title: Require side-effect-safe timeout ownership
options.body: Block merge until timed-out OAuth and runtime auth operations cannot persist credentials or mutate active auth state after their lock or single-flight ownership has ended.

options.title: Accept deadline-only mitigation
options.body: Merge the current approach as an availability mitigation while explicitly accepting late credential and runtime-auth write risk.

options.title: Pause for auth-owner redesign
options.body: Hold this branch until an auth owner supplies a concrete cancellation or generation-guard design plus runtime proof.

recommendation.title: Require side-effect-safe timeout ownership
recommendation.body: Block merge until timed-out OAuth and runtime auth operations cannot persist credentials or mutate active auth state after their lock or single-flight ownership has ended.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current-main history across both auth-controller and OAuth manager surfaces touched by the risk.
